newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GRAF, COETZER BOOK QUARTER-FINAL REMATCH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF, COETZER BOOK QUARTER-FINAL REMATCH.

text.p: Steffi Graf overcame a blustery wind and Romania's Irina Spirlea to move into the French Open quarter-finals for the 12th successive year on Sunday.

Seeded number two, Graf's 6-7 6-2 6-2 victory on a windswept centre court set the stage for a quarter-final clash with South Africa's Amanda Coetzer who prevailed in an equally demanding three-setter over 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez of Spain.

The tiny South African has had the German's number this season, beating her in two of their three meetings, including an embarrassing 6-0 6-1 drubbing at the German Open and a straight sets fourth round win at the Australian Open.
Graf, however, is almost a permanent fixture in the final eight at Roland Garros, having won the title five times and reached the final on three other occasions.

Still wearing a bandage on the injured left knee which sidelined her for three months, Graf took time to warm up on a cool, windy day, dropping her first set of the tournament to the 13th seeded Spirlea in a tie-break.
It was the first time Graf had been forced to come back from one set down to win a match at Roland Garros since 1993.

Romania will however, be represented in the quarter-finals, Ruxandra Dragomir crushing American Nicole Arendt 6-1 6-1 to book her place in the last eight where she will meet Iva Majoli, a 5-7 6-4 6-2 winner over American Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport.
"It was difficult for me to get into the match because of the conditions, it was very windy out there," said Graf. "In the next two sets I found my rhythm and started playing better.
"I feel I'm moving better than I have been in the last few weeks.
"It's good to win a tough match, I feel confident."
Despite Graf's mounting confidence, Coetzer's 6-7 6-4 6-3 win over Martinez will not come as welcome news.
In a match that changed directions as many times as the gusty wind, Coetzer showed impressive resolve to record her first win in a 11 meetings with the Spaniard .
"It was tough, extremely windy, at times it was even tough to see," said Coetzer. "I rank this up there among my best wins.
"Before today I had never beaten her, I don't think I had even taken a set from her."

After breezing through her opening three matches without dropping a set, Coetzer looked ready to cruise into the final eight at Roland Garros for the second straight year as she jumped to a 5-2 lead in the first set.

But Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon champion, stormed back to take a 6-5 lead, forcing Coetzer to fight off six set points before going to a tie-break. The Spaniard eventually took the set in one hour and 22 minutes.
The battle continued to fluctuate in the decisive set, the two women trading breaks twice before Coetzer finally wrested control to end Martinez's bid for a ninth consecutive semifinal appearance.

While Coetzer's appearance in the next round is not a major surprise, the same cannot be said about qualifier Filip Dewulf who became the first Belgian to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final in the Open era with his stunning 5-7 6-1 6-4 7-5 over the eighth seeded Corretja.
Dewulf, ranked 122 in the world, took advantage of the Spaniard's uncertainty in the windy conditions to clinch the most significant win of his career in two hours and 57 minutes.

"I came here to play the qualifying and I'm in the quarter-finals, it's totally unexpected," said Dewulf, who had never advanced beyond the second round previous Grand Slam events. "I gave my all because I had nothing to lose."
He now meets Swede Magnus Norman who upset 15th seed Marc Rosset 4-6 6-3 7-6 6-3 to reduce the number of men's seeds left in the draw to four.
